messages:
rachel: Heads-up: a subset of streaming JSON payloads are getting truncated when SSE chunks split mid-object after an upstream gzip/coalesce step. Clients see JSON.parse errors and immediately reconnect.

nick: Oof. Splitting in the middle of a JSON object would definitely break our incremental parser. Any samples?
rachel: Example payload sequence (simplified):
```
chunk1: '{"type":"message","id":123,"body":"hello wor'
chunk2: 'ld","meta":{"k":"v"}}\n\n'
```
Client receives chunk1 then chunk2 but our SSE framing expects full event per chunk; parser treats chunk1 as complete -> parse error.

li: So root cause = proxy/cdn merging/splitting event bodies unpredictably. Short-term: make client parser tolerant by buffering until a JSON object closes (count braces) OR add an invariant: server adds Content-Length-like field in event to indicate byte-length. Which is easier short-term?

rachel: Buffering on client is quick to roll out (feature flag) but we need to detect malicious streams that never close. Suggest max-buffer 16KB + timeout 5s. Emit metric stream.json.fragment.drop when we hit timeout.

nick: Server-side change (explicit length header) is more robust but requires widespread rollout across proxies and gateways. Longer timeline.

ops-bot: Deploy queued: rachel/client-json-buffer -> canary eu-central-1.

li: Also add telemetry: stream.json.fragment.count and stream.json.fragment.timeout. Add Grafana panel and alert if fragment.count > 20/min regionally.

rachel: Canary (3m): client-buffering reduced parse errors by 92% on canary cohort. No memory spike; some clients hit 5s buffer timeout for malformed streams. stream.json.fragment.timeout fired for those.

nick: Great. Follow-ups: (1) client buffer rollout behind flag and gradual ramp (rachel) (2) RFC for server content-length in SSE events (nick) (3) dashboard tiles + alert (li).

li: I'll land the Grafana panel and add an ops-runbook snippet on how to distinguish true truncation vs malicious slow streams.

rachel: Added console note to hide transient reconnects from product-facing session counts while we stabilize.

nick: If we see buffer timeouts concentrated by CDN edge, we should push the content-length header there first.

ops-bot: Canary deployed: rachel/client-json-buffer -> eu-central-1.

rachel: Will promote after 30m stable. Closing thread unless anyone sees new parse spikes.
